answer:
I wrote `plans/plain-drop-status-2.json` with no steps, on purpose. The task says `orders.status` isn't used any more, but the running app still uses it, so dropping it now would cause an outage.

**Why I didn't drop it:**
- `app/server.js:28` writes `status` on every new order (`INSERT INTO orders (..., status, email) VALUES (..., 'new', $3)`).
- `app/server.js:30` reads it on every `GET /order/ID` (`SELECT id, customer_id, ..., status, email`).
- The live database confirms this: orders created seconds before I checked all have `status = 'new'`.
- None of the settings (`AMOUNT_READ`, `AMOUNT_WRITE`, `GUEST_EMAIL`) turns `status` off, so a `deploy` step can't fix it.

If the plan dropped the column, every new order and every order lookup would fail with "column status does not exist" across all three replicas, straight away.

**What it would take:**
1. Change the app code: remove `status` from `insertSql` and `readSql` and roll that out. (Live, `status` is already nullable, so inserts without it will work.)
2. Then a one-step plan: `SET lock_timeout = '2s'; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN status;`. This is a quick change that doesn't rewrite the 10M rows. The lock timeout stops it from holding up the app's queries if it has to wait for a lock.

Once an app version without `status` is deployed, I can write that plan.
